title: Team Skill Capped by Weakest Stamina
statement:
There are n candidates. Candidate i has skill[i] and stamina[i]. Pick a team of exactly k different candidates.

A team's output is the sum of its skills multiplied by the smallest stamina in the team: the whole team can only work as long as its weakest member lasts. Return the largest output any team can reach.

examples.why: Candidates 0 and 2: (2 + 4) · min(5, 3) = 18. Taking the two most skilled, 7 and 4, gives only 11 · 1, because candidate 1 has stamina 1.
With one member, the output is that member's skill times their own stamina. The best is 3 · 9.
Everyone must be in the team: 8 · 4.

gen: (r, big) => { const n = big ? 100000 : r.int(1, 8); return [r.arr(n, 0, big ? 100000 : 9), r.arr(n, 0, big ? 100000 : 9), big ? r.int(1, n) : r.int(1, n)]; }
hints: Two things interact: the sum and the minimum. What if you fix which candidate holds the minimum stamina?
Sort candidates by stamina, highest first. When you reach candidate i, everyone seen so far has stamina ≥ stamina[i], so if i is in the team, its stamina is the cap.
For that cap you want the k − 1 largest skills among the candidates already seen, plus skill[i]. A min-heap of size k keeps the k largest skills seen so far and their sum.

explain.intuition:
The minimum is the awkward part, so take it out of the picture: decide who the weakest member is. Sort by stamina, highest first, and walk down the list. When you are at candidate i, every candidate before it has at least its stamina, so a team built from i and earlier candidates is capped exactly at stamina[i] (or at something no larger, which only underestimates and is covered when that weaker member is reached).

For a fixed cap, the best team simply has the largest possible skill sum among the eligible candidates. That is a "top k so far" question, which a min-heap of size k answers as the list grows: push each new skill, and when the heap holds more than k, drop the smallest. The heap's running sum times the current stamina is a candidate answer.
steps: Sort candidate indices by stamina, descending.
Walk them in that order. Push the skill into a min-heap and add it to sum.
If the heap has more than k skills, pop the smallest and subtract it from sum.
When the heap has exactly k skills, update the answer with sum · stamina[i].
pitfalls: Picking the k most skilled candidates and ignoring stamina, as the first example shows.
Scoring before pushing the current candidate. Then a team that contains it, capped by its own stamina, is never scored, and later caps are only lower.
Overflowing 32-bit integers: the product can reach 10¹⁵.

solutions.title: Every team of size k
solutions.idea: Enumerate all k-subsets, tracking the skill sum and the minimum stamina. Exponential; only for small n.

solutions.title: Sort by stamina, min-heap of skills
solutions.idea: Fix the weakest member by walking stamina from high to low. Keep the k largest skills seen so far in a min-heap with a running sum.

followups: Team size can be anything up to k instead of exactly k. What changes?
Use the sum of staminas and the minimum skill instead. Is it the same problem?
